sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx:Quality Checks!31 and Internal Quality Checks!31
evidence: The frozen workbook Quality Checks row 31 requires every rejection/absence check to have a matching success case; quality-checks.md:127-129 specifies that the control belongs in the same criterion. Functional judge.toml:167 begins cw_error_message_and_line with a valid JavaScript Run, then grades both JavaScript and complete HTML inline-script errors. It does not require a successful inline HTML script Run before the HTML error check. The separate cw_html_preview at lines 152-159 does exercise valid HTML, but functional/prompt.md:1,5 scores rows independently and says a prior row failure must not erase independent evidence; cw_error_message_and_line does not require the judge to reuse a directly observed HTML success. Other important negative checks do include relevant controls: timeout has a working short timer (line 185), preview boundary has own-preview DOM/console and harmless-word controls (line 194), and stale Save has A's valid Save and a fresh server read (line 212). The public behaviour.md asks for errors inside complete HTML files, so the missing HTML control bears on a required behavior. This is a source-level finding. raw-evidence-index.json was absent when checked, and no actual judge or broken-app run was available to verify score impact.
counterexample: A partially broken app executes ordinary JavaScript but never executes inline scripts in complete HTML. It scans HTML source for a throw statement and prints the copied message with a calculated line number. It can satisfy the valid JavaScript control and the two error readouts in cw_error_message_and_line while failing actual HTML script execution. A conforming app executes a benign inline HTML script first, shows its DOM/console effect, and then reports the deliberate inline-script error at the authored source line.
suggested_fix: In cw_error_message_and_line, require a successful complete-HTML inline-script control with an observed DOM or console effect before attempting the HTML error; keep the JavaScript control and require both controls as direct observations for this criterion.
